traps: AC ids are the prose paragraphs under 'Requirements' in source order: AC-1 empty-form messages, AC-2 verify-account mismatch, AC-3 non-numeric account/amount, AC-4 success confirmation, AC-5 balance decrease, AC-6 Find Transactions by amount (+ 'Invalid amount'), AC-7 REST transactions by amount, AC-8 REST billpay then found in the UI, AC-9 payee reached by next business day.

AC-9 ('reach the payee no later than the next business day') cannot be verified black-box: ParaBank has no payee side or settlement status. The evaluator must surface it as not verifiable / open question (-> PASS_WITH_WARNINGS), not invent a check and not FAIL it.

Bill Pay validation is client-side jQuery bound on document ready; clicking 'Send Payment' immediately after navigation (before the script binds) shows no messages at all (observed once). Wait for load/network idle; an empty-message result from an early click is a script defect, not an AC-1 deviation.

Mixed input such as '12abc' passes the page's parseFloat check, reaches the service (400) and shows 'Error! An internal error has occurred and has been logged.' The story only covers letters-only input ('ten', 'abcd'), which is met; a '12abc' probe is outside the stated criteria and must not be reported as an AC-3 deviation (at most an observation).
The REST billpay service accepts an empty payee ({}) and records 'Bill Payment to null' (probed) — REST payee validation is not a requirement of this story; not a deviation.

The phone input has a random id/class per page load (e.g. id='ec127bf3-...'); locate fields by name (payee.name, payee.address.street, payee.phoneNumber, payee.accountNumber, verifyAccount, amount, fromAccountId).
'Account number is required.' appears twice on the empty form (Account # and Verify Account #) — expected per AC-1.

Find Transactions: an amount with no match shows the 'Transaction Results' table with no rows (no message); that is not specified and is fine. Dates are epoch-ms at UTC midnight rendered in browser local time; do not assert the date.
The UI and REST amount path uses the number as typed after parseFloat (37.10 -> /amount/37.1); REST /transactions/amount/37.10 also works.
Use a unique payee name and amount per test so Find by amount is deterministic within the fresh customer's account.
POST /billpay takes accountId and amount as query parameters and the Payee JSON {name, address{street,city,state,zipCode}, phoneNumber, accountNumber} as the body with Content-Type application/json.

AC-2: only 'The account numbers do not match.' and no payment (probed).
AC-3: 'Please enter a valid number.' (per account field) and 'Please enter a valid amount.' for 'abcd'/'ten'; no payment (probed).
AC-4: 'Bill Payment Complete' / 'Bill Payment to qa-author Water Co in the amount of $37.10 from account 21336 was successful.' for input 37.1 (probed).
AC-6: row 'Bill Payment to <payee>' with $37.10 in Debit (-); 'ten' -> 'Invalid amount' (probed).
AC-7: 200 [{type Debit, amount 37.10, description 'Bill Payment to qa-author Water Co'}]; 99.99 -> 200 [] (probed).
AC-8: POST /billpay -> 200 {payeeName, amount 18.40, accountId}; found on Find Transactions by 18.40 (probed).
